title: Cheeky Malware Linked To Popular Gacha Game Cracks City Security
description: East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments. One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident. Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC. The subcontractor in question, IT services company GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had launched the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment." Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

title: GTA 6 Players Captivated By Mandy Apparently Include A Former Nintendo President
description: A character named Mandy has the attention of many Grand Theft Auto 6 players--and that appears to include Reggie Fils-Aimé, the man who used to run Nintendo of America. Per GamesRadar, former Nintendo marketing and public relations manager Krysta Yang joked on social media that GTA 6, which is front-loaded with a lot of simulation-like busywork in the first chapter, is "adult Animal Crossing," posting images that highlight parallels between GTA 6 and Animal Crossing: New Horizons. Fils-Aimé quoted the post, saying: "If so, where's Mandy?" It's slightly eyebrow raising that the former executive for a family-friendly company like Nintendo seems to have a strong opinion for a rather promiscuous video game character. No judgment to Fils-Aimé, of course, but talk around Mandy carries a certain... tone. Minor spoilers for the early parts of GTA 6 follow. One of the earliest missions in GTA 6 has Jason stopping by Mandy's home to collect rent. Long story short, she flirts pretty aggressively with Jason, who clearly isn't reciprocating, and Mandy doesn't take it well. And no, even if players wanted to, you can't romance Mandy. It doesn't help that it's implied that Mandy carries a dark secret, with Jason discovering a severed finger while fixing her sink's pipes. I'm not sure if anyone in Animal Crossing is that shady. So what does this post say about Reggie Fils-Aimé as a person? It's unclear what he thinks of the character--all we know is that he'd really like to know who the Animal Crossing equivalent of Mandy would be. It certainly wouldn't be Isabelle, so take your pick of any weird villagers you've encountered. Either way, it seems that Fils-Aimé is playing GTA 6 like the rest of us or, at the very least, is in tune with the massive cultural zeitgeist the game has produced.

GTA 6 Is Out, And People Are Planning To Party–Outside The Game In A Much Different World
description: Rockstar Games finally released Grand Theft Auto 6 on Thursday. The game was highly anticipated because of, well, a lot of reasons. It’s a technical marvel that can simulate anything from doomscrolling on your phone to the thrill of hitting the club in the Miami-inspired Vice City. But it's not just about what you can do in the game. Since its release, a new viral trend on social media has emerged: People are saying they are going out, hitting the bar, and dancing--all in the real world--now that men are inside playing GTA 6. Now that Rockstar Games has released GTA 6, a lot of cisgender men won’t be going clubbing or be out in general. (They will be inside playing the game instead.) That will give people—especially women, femmes, and nonbinary people—the perfect chance to go out and have a fun time at the bar by themselves. The videos vary slightly but are all riffing on how it could be the perfect weekend for these groups to go out in a world without men. In one video posted on Wednesday, the Instagram user Laurenblackborow talks about why it will be nice for women to hit the town this weekend. “Ladies, if you’ve ever dreamed of a world where men do not exist and we can walk around at night and not fear for our lives, tomorrow is the night. Because men are predictable and every single man is gonna be playing GTA 6. The world is our oyster,” Laurenblackborow said. The video has more than 10,000 likes and has been viewed more than 194,000 times. Other videos simply joke about how tranquil life will be or how empty the gym will be. Anna, a model based in Germany, is another woman who posted about Grand Theft Auto 6. Her video, which has more than 67,500 likes and 770,000 views, consists of a montage of women hitting the town with text that says, “Girls night out this weekend because all men will be indoors on gta6.” You can see women shaking ass and enjoying themselves as “TikTok” by Kesha plays in the background. Anna told GameSpot she wasn’t going out specifically…

title: How To Play Golf (And Mini-Golf) In GTA 6
description: Golf is one of the most popular sports in the real state of Florida, so it's no surprise that Grand Theft Auto 6 offers plenty of ways to play golf in the fictional state of Leonida. GTA 6 offers two types of golf: mini-golf and traditional 18-hole golf, both of which are fully accessible from the start of the game. Leonida also features multiple courses for whichever version of golf you decide to play. There are some slightly different rules for mini-golf versus regular golf, but the mechanics for either of them will make sense after a couple of holes. Below, you can see all of the golf course locations in GTA 6 and how to play like a pro. The course locations are fairly spread out in Leonida, and the mini-golf courses all feature different themes, making the holes look and feel extremely varied. You can see the names and locations for all five of the golf courses in GTA 6 below: Traditional Golf Courses Leaf Links Golf Club Located just north of Washington Beach, this location returns from the original Vice City. In GTA 6, Leaf Links is its own island, centered around a full 18-hole golf course with sprawling ocean views and some of the wealthiest houses in all of Leonida. Though Mar-a-Lago doesn't seem to be in the game, this course probably comes closest to capturing its vibe. Check the bathrooms for classified documents. Mount Hailes Club Located in north Waning Sands, Mount Hailes Club is a well-maintained course that feels like a standard country club golf experience. title: GTA 6 Has Dexter References, And Now Dexter Himself Has Reacted
description: Actor Michael C. Hall has reacted to how GTA 6 features references to his Miami-set TV show Dexter, in which he famously played the serial killer Dexter. Appearing on the Barstool Movies show, Hall said he was "informed" of the Easter eggs in GTA 6 about his character. "I wasn't consulted," he said with a laugh. "It's pretty cool to feel like [Dexter] has folded into the zeitgeist." After the GTA 6 Extended Look premiered in August, people immediately spotted what they thought was Dexter's apartment building from the TV show. Now that GTA 6 has arrived, people found the apartment building in the game, and you can, too, by following GameSpot's Dexter apartment guide here. On the TV show, Dexter dismembers his victims, stuffs them into garbage bags, and dumps them into the nearby harbor on his boat, the Slice of Life. Players can also get into a kill house that bears a resemblance to the one that Dexter uses on the show, complete with plastic sheets for the blood splatter, hammers, and cleavers. Players have also found bones underwater, presumably another reference to Dexter. GTA 6 is full of Easter eggs, so be sure to check out GameSpot's breakdown of GTA 6's best Easter eggs to seek out while you're traveling around Vice City. GTA 6 launched on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S, and it sold more than 32 million copies and brought in close to $4 billion in revenue by day one. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

title: GTA 6 Sets Even More Records
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release. For starters, the internet service provider Comcast announced that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the company's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network. GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast said around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the New Zealand trick ). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said. A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight. Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster. Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox. These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said. For…

title: GTA 6’s Astonishing $4 Billion Day One Includes 32.5 Million Copies Sold
description: GTA 6 is an enormous hit--it's the biggest gaming release ever. Take-Two just announced that GTA 6 reach 32.5 million copies sold before release, with revenue reaching $3.79 billion through the end of the first day on sale on November 19. This makes it the biggest entertainment release--for any medium--in history, Take-Two said. For comparison, 2013's GTA 5 hit $800 million in revenue in its first 24 hours and $1 billion after its first three days, so GTA 6 is pacing well ahead of those numbers. GTA 5 launched at $60, compared to $80 for the cheapest version of GTA 6. For comparison, the all-time highest-grossing movie ever is Avengers: Endgame, which made $2.94 billion during its entire run. GTA 6 has done nearly $1 billion more in revenue already. According to reporter Jason Schreier, GTA 6 is also now instantly one of the top 30 best-selling games of all time. “It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI,” Rockstar president and co-founder Sam Houser said. “We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn’t be more excited to share this moment with you.” Big numbers for GTA 6 were always expected. Sensor Tower had been sharing unofficial sales data for GTA 6 for a long time already, but Take-Two's sales numbers are even higher than the 25 million sales that Sensor Tower reported at launch. GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

title: You Should Bike More (In GTA 6)
description: I'm several hours into Rockstar's behemoth video game, and as big as the GTA 6 map is, I've seldom needed (and even less often preferred) more than two wheels to get around. Biking in GTA 6 is awesome, and it's a safe bet to say you should be doing it more than you are. Sure, Grand Theft Auto 6 might imply heavy use of automobiles right there in its title, and there are plenty of amazing boats, planes, and cars to find--heck, there's even a tank. But none of these other ways to get from A to B really compare to a good old-fashioned bicycle. I'm an avid biker in real life, so I wasted no time taking Jason's bike (found beneath his back deck in Chapter 1) for a joyride when I was given free rein of the open world. Quickly, I realized GTA bicycles have a number of benefits, many of which mirror real life, but a few are exclusive to the game, too. For one, every time you travel via bicycle, you're saving on gas. Gas prices in GTA 6 are as painful as they are in real life right now, and since you do have to fill up your car with gas once in a while, biking minimizes the number of trips you'll need to take to the nearest gas station. I actually haven't used a gas station yet because of all the biking I'm doing. Jason's bike spawns just behind his shed at his Chapter 1 safehouse. Since one of the best GTA 6 tips we can offer is to establish healthy habits, biking also doubles as a workout. Whenever you're biking, even if you're not speeding up (by pressing A/X on Xbox or PlayStation, respectively), you're contributing to a cardio workout. This is a fantastic way to multitask, since it can be hard to fit a gym routine into Jason and Lucia's busy lives. I was worried at first that I wouldn't be able to listen to music while biking. I didn't want to sacrifice the eclectic list of GTA 6 songs. Thankfully, Rockstar doesn't make me pick one or the other. If you buy in-ear headphones, you can use them even if you're biking and wearing your helmet. On that note, you should…

title: GTA 6’s Auto-Drive Feature Is Easy To Miss But Extremely Handy
description: GTA 6 may still very much be a Grand Theft Auto game, but some fundamental changes--a stronger focus on realism, money being scarce --do a lot to shake things up. Driving might not feel totally different, but the decision-making behind choosing what to drive and how reckless to be on the road give that portion of the game a much different feel. But should you prefer not to drive yourself, you do have a choice, and it doesn't involve taking taxis or relying on public transportation. It can be easy to miss, due to how it's accessed, but there is an auto-drive option you can enable so your current character drives themselves. Here's how to enable it: Hold Down on the D-Pad while in a vehicle Press Options/Start to enable Cinematic Mode Hold Circle/B to turn on auto-drive By default, your character will seemingly just drive themselves around aimlessly. However, if you set a destination on the map, they'll instead drive there. That's useful not just on the roads, but also with other vehicle types. For instance, you can hop on a boat and mark the location for a diving mission, and spare yourself the oft-uneventful process of manually driving to it. Cinematic Mode gives you nice camera angles from which to enjoy the visuals, and not having to pay attention to where you're driving means you can spend more time gawking at all of the details littered throughout the world. Or you can just pretend you're the passenger and enjoy playing with the radio, without having to spend exorbitant sums on a taxi ride. Auto-drive can be canceled at any time, so you're not locked into a full trip if something catches your attention along the way. One thing you can't do is play around on your phone while in auto-drive. To do that, you'll need to be manually driving, which means getting pulled into a first-person perspective that makes the prospect even more precarious. While in auto-drive, you can adjust between three speed settings depending on the urgency with which you want Jason or Lucia…

title: GTA 6 Has The Best Use Of PS5’s DualSense Controller Yet
description: I expected Xbox Series X|S's Quick Resume to be the defining feature of this console generation, but it's been the unique features offered by PS5's DualSense controller that have actually provided the biggest edge for me. GTA 6 is not only the latest such example of this, but it's also the best example of leveraging the DualSense yet. The controller's speaker is used for some nice touches, like hearing your phone ring or chatter on the police scanner, but as is often the case, it's the DualSense triggers that make the more meaningful difference. These are leveraged in myriad ways that can significantly enhance the experience of whatever you're doing. For instance, the home-repair tasks you can complete early in the game see the triggers react differently based on what you're doing. It just feels more immersive for the triggers to not behave normally when you're installing screws with a driver; that's an action that should not feel identical to firing a gun or hitting the gas in your car. Similarly, there's an added weight to the strength-training activities you can take part in that lend an added sense that Jason and Lucia are actually picking up heavy items, not just manipulating weightless objects made of 1s and 0s. But where I think the DualSense triggers really shine is in driving. The triggers have a soft lock that allow you to pull and maintain a speed that is appropriate for the road you're on. Certainly in the early hours, when money is at a premium and alternative vehicles are not easy to steal, keeping your car in good shape is made easier by obeying traffic laws, and that is easier if you can comfortably pull the trigger without maxing out the RPMs. You can just as easily pull the trigger past that point to put the pedal to the floor and go as fast as you want, but that little bit of resistance lends that dangerous decision a bit of extra excitement, almost like a piece of physical feedback that you're choosing to break the law.
